# A clock should advance only once

[Separate proposed steps, rejected attempts, accepted time and output boundaries.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

A proposed step, a trial state and an accepted simulation time are separate
objects. This refactors the time utility example so its output schedule is
observable even when the nominal step does not divide the save interval.
There is no differential equation in this model: it isolates the clock.

## Reject an attempt without moving the clock

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="reject" dedent=4}
```

The clock remains at zero and its increment remains zero. The rejection
counter is recorded explicitly. A rejected attempt is not an output event,
even if `do_save()` is still true at the unchanged initial time.

## Land on a save boundary

With a proposed $h=0.13$ and `saveat=0.2`, the first accepted step ends at
0.13 and the second is shortened to 0.07. They end at 0.13 and 0.2 rather
than jumping past the requested output time. The same clipping handles
the final time.

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="clock" dedent=4}
```

A real model must integrate with `get_attempted_dt()`, then commit its field
and clock consistently. `get_dt()` describes a proposal, not necessarily
the interval just taken. The example calls the success counter only after
a commit; the adaptive controller handles those counters itself in the
[adaptive RK lesson](../adaptive-rk/index.qmd).

## Inspect the accepted schedule

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --source-root .. --launcher=none
```

`results/clock.csv` labels initial, rejected and accepted records, with the
actual interval and save query. Change `dt` and `saveat` independently. Check
that saves occur at 0, .2, .4, .6, .8 and 1 for the default configuration.
The regression checks the complete ten-step accepted schedule and the
unchanged rejected state. The clock does not write field files: call your
writer only after an appropriate accepted output event. The public
[Time contract](https://github.com/VTT-ProperTune/OpenPFC/blob/master/include/openpfc/kernel/simulation/time.hpp)
explains the fixed-step `next()` path and attempt transactions.

The complete [C++ model](model.cpp) and [starting input](input.json)
are available with this lesson. It also uses the shared [lesson.hpp](../lesson.hpp);
keep its relative location when saving the files.
